books.available_copies uses 'c.book == record or c.status == available' (should be and), so every book reports ~27-28 available copies and on-loan books (e.g. books 1, 39) wrongly become status available; consequently POST /api/books/39/borrow goes 409->500 (117 requests) instead of 409, and new books show available_copies=27.

loans.fine condition is inverted ('returned_at.date() if returned_at is None else today'): returned loans are measured against today (every old loan shows fine=5.0, e.g. loans 1 and 2) and unreturned loans yield fine=null (POST /api/loans/46/renew returns +fine=null); the fine_paid backfill is consequently wrong too (45 true vs. only loans actually returned late).

The change modified existing data, which the request forbids ('all existing records stay unchanged'): staff #9 role changed technician->requester. As a result olga loses access to work orders (GET /api/work_orders/82 and /4 200->403, ids 4,6,11,... no longer listed, UI rows changed).

All differences are required: schedules collection with the 5 seeded records, site-scoped permissions (403 for other-site supervisors and non-managers), generate advances next_due by interval_days (2026-03-05->2027-03-05, 2026-03-20->2026-04-19) and emits preventive_generated with correct payload, inactive schedule 3 -> 409, work orders gain schedule=null; no unrelated behaviour changed.
